target.title: feat(qa): add transport capability and factory contracts
target.body:
Fixes #99622

## What Problem This Solves

QA Lab selected QA Channel and Crabline adapters through separate static and special-case paths. Canonical scenarios could not declare transport requirements, adapter capabilities were not versioned or machine-readable, and missing capabilities or unsupported operations did not share a closed error contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change adds one asynchronous `QaTransportAdapterFactory` registry for the existing QA Channel and Crabline adapters. Factories expose a versioned capability manifest, validate requested capabilities before adapter startup, verify declared operations against the created adapter, and normalize missing-capability, startup, credential-blocked, and unsupported-operation failures.

Scenario execution metadata now accepts `execution.transport.requiredCapabilities`. The existing channel streaming scenario declares text and preview-lifecycle requirements while retaining the established `waitForOutboundSequence` flow. Factory and suite cleanup covers capability rejection, adapter startup, provider startup, and Gateway startup failures.

The contract stays inside the QA Lab plugin boundary and consumes the existing `@openclaw/crabline@0.1.8` adapter/server API. Script evidence writing and scenario catalog ownership validation are unchanged.

## User Impact

No direct end-user behavior changes. QA maintainers and channel contributors get deterministic transport preflight, machine-readable capability declarations, consistent blocked/failure errors, and one adapter creation path for QA Channel and Crabline scenarios.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/qa-transport-contracts.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/qa-transport-registry.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-catalog.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-flow.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/suite.test.ts` — 5 files, 63 tests passed.
- Scoped `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` passed for all touched TypeScript files.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwmp6bm3xerp0nmys08xfwdm` — `check:changed` passed, including full typecheck, core/extensions/scripts lint, and runtime import-cycle validation.
- Codex autoreview — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Existing-solutions preflight found no maintained generic registry package that supplied the repository-specific transport lifecycle, capability manifest, and normalized error contract; the implementation reuses current QA Lab registry patterns and Crabline's published bridge API.
